_notes:
Adafruit NeoSlider (product 5295): seesaw firmware on an ATtiny817 (hardware ID 0x87) at 0x30, the default (A0-A3 jumpers give 0x31-0x3F, not claimed: a seesaw detection writes two bytes, which other chips there would take as a register and data). Seesaw registers are a module base and a function
Detection: STATUS_VERSION (0x00 0x02), 5 ms, 4 bytes: the top 16 bits are the Adafruit product number, 5295 (0x14AF), the rest a date code
Init: STATUS_SWRST (0x00 0x7F = 0xFF), 20 ms (turns its NeoPixels off)
Poll (100 ms): ADC channel for pin 18, the slider (0x09 0x07+18 = 0x19), 5 ms, 2 bytes big-endian, 0-1023. The 4 NeoPixels (pin 14) aren't driven
Source: pins and registers from Adafruit's seesaw library and NeoSlider examples; the version and timings checked on the bench

rsao.note: bench (Axiom018, 2026-11-08): the lone 0x99 returns 0xFF and the next ADC reads are normal
